newsitem.title: USA: Times Mirror sees slower EPS growth ahead.
newsitem.headline: Times Mirror sees slower EPS growth ahead.

text.p: Times Mirror Co said Thursday it expects the rate of its earnings growth to slow in the second half of 1997.
Chairman, President and Chief Executive Mark Willes said in a statement that the rate of growth could slow "somewhat" because of anticipated increases in newsprint prices.
In addition, during that period, "we will continue to incur consolidation expenses in our professional information segment," he said.
For the first six months of 1997, the company reported net income of $111.2 million, or $0.94 per share, on revenues of $1.586 billion.
In the same period in the prior year, Times Mirror posted net income of $72.1 million, or $0.47 per share, on revenues of $1.644 billion.
